_status: NFS's historical vendor assessments, transcribed from knowledge/historical-vendor-assessments/*.pdf. Cite them via source_document.

key_findings: The initial incident-notification commitment was 72 hours; contract negotiation reduced it to 24 hours.
Production use was approved only after the contract amendment.
conditions: Contract amendment reducing incident notification from 72 to 24 hours, before production use
assessments.lesson_learned: Contractual remediation can convert some policy gaps into acceptable residual risk when the vendor can meet the mandatory requirement before go-live.

key_findings: The vendor retained Confidential prompts for 90 days.
The vendor reserved the right to use customer content to improve models.
assessments.lesson_learned: Rejected because mandatory AI data-use and retention requirements could not be met.

key_findings: The vendor met encryption and identity requirements.
SOC 2 evidence was missing from the assessment package and recorded as UNKNOWN.
A temporary pilot using Internal data only was allowed while evidence was obtained.
conditions: Pilot restricted to Internal data until SOC 2 evidence is provided
assessments.lesson_learned: Missing evidence is UNKNOWN, not PASS. Scope restriction can enable a controlled pilot without approving higher-risk data processing.
